transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, I guess I came in because I keep getting these nagging thoughts at work. I'm a designer, and... well, I just keep worrying that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or maybe that I sent the wrong version of a file to a client. And even when I look at it and I can clearly see it’s probably fine, my mind just keeps circling back to it anyway. It's just getting really frustrating to deal with.

When you have these thoughts, do you feel compelled to perform any specific actions, like double-checking the files repeatedly or counting or repeating words in your head, to try to make the worry go away?

Yeah, I do. Um, before I submit my work now, I'll actually re-open the file just to be sure. I go in and compare all the layers, re-save it, and... sometimes I'll just sit there and mentally walk through every single design choice I made one more time. It doesn't take over my whole day or anything, so I can still get things done. But it definitely makes me slower, and I just feel a lot less free creatively when I'm stuck doing all that checking.
Do you find that you have these persistent, unwanted worries about things completely unrelated to your job, such as fears about your health, your personal safety, or the safety of your loved ones?

No, not really. It's pretty much just focused on my work. I don't really worry about getting sick or anything happening to my family, at least not any more than a normal person would. It's just the design files and the client stuff that gets me stuck. Outside of work, I feel pretty normal.
Do you feel that your need to repeatedly check your work is excessive or unreasonable, even though you feel compelled to do it anyway?

Yeah, I do think it's unreasonable. I mean, I know I'm good at my job, and I know I've checked the file already. It's just... I can't seem to stop myself from doing it again. It feels excessive because I know it's not actually necessary, but I just get this urge that I have to do it anyway just to feel okay about sending it off.
About how much time, on an average day, do you find yourself spending on these repeated checks before you finally feel like you can move on?

Um, I'm not entirely sure exactly how much time it adds up to. I haven't really timed it or anything. I guess if I had to estimate, maybe... an extra twenty or thirty minutes a day? It's usually just a few extra minutes here and there before I send off an email or finalize a project, so it's not like I'm losing hours at a time. It just kind of drags the process out a bit.
How long have you been experiencing these repetitive checking behaviors, and have they been present for at least several months?

I'm not exactly sure when it started, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of a specific timeline. It's been going on for a while, I guess, but I couldn't say for certain if it's been several months or not. It just feels like something I've been dealing with lately.
Outside of your work, do you find that you frequently experience a sense of excessive worry or tension about a variety of different life events or daily activities?

No, not really. I mean, I get stressed sometimes like anyone else, but... I wouldn't say I'm constantly worried or tense about regular life stuff. It's pretty much just that specific checking thing with my design files at work. When I'm at home or just doing everyday things, I feel fine.
